title: Trumpet and trombone changes: Shad Collins, Harry Edison, Dickie Wells, Benny Morton
summary: Jones traces who joined the brass in 1937-38 as the band grew to four trumpets and three trombones.

story.theme_name: Who was in the band: naming sidemen and personnel
story.community_name: Who played in the band: reciting personnel

blocks.x: If you have the records I'm sure it's there. There were some other guys in that - Joe Keyes and Carl Smith and Buck Clayton were in the band now. When did Shad Collins and other guys begin to come into the band? Shad was in there, wasn't he?
Shad joined us in 1938. See we had a series of trumpet players.
You don't know whose place he took?

Well, you see there was a whole lot of shuffling going on because remember we had a little fellow by the name of Bobby Moore, a little 17-year-old wonder, who was the forerunner of Dizzy Gillespie. He joined us in '37. He was a kid and he went to get an operation on his teeth and before he could heal well - we didn't have time to wait on him to heal - that's when Harry Edison came in in 1938. But Shad, when we did the thing at Randall's Island - that was the big festival that they had at Randall's Island with Martin Block. Duke Ellington opened up the concert. They had a great big festival out there; you had Kay Kyser, you had the whole big bands out there. Dickie Wells was -
When did Dickie come in now -
Dickie and Shad came in together. Then going into - oh, we did our one-nighters and things like that. Dan Minor was still there.
We finally added the third trombone because Dickie Wells, Dan Minor, and Mr. Benny Morton. We put him in.
Now did you add a trumpet because you only had 3 trumpets?

We had Buck Clayton, Ed Lewis, Shad Collins, and Harry Edison. We had four trumpets now. Now we're building up the brass section; reed sections stay the same. Then we begin to build up and here you had Benny Morton, you had Dan Minor, you know -
That makes for a brass section -
